title: Advance expired multiplayer phases once with seeded deadline completion
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md, docs/design/SWARM-BRIEF-v0.md, docs/design/RULES-SPEC-v1.md and the listed sourceRefs before editing. The imported Rules Spec v1 is the canonical engine contract; the earlier prototype/T01-T10 interfaces are baseline compatibility, not current gameplay rules. Do not restore approval votes, Repair/Sabotage buttons, Witness or five-node tracks. Preserve original IP and engine independence from Firebase/UI/Node. Edit only ownership; publish APIs only through explicitly owned package entrypoints, preserving baseline exports. Use original synthetic fixtures, scoped tests/lint/typecheck and npm run check. Do not commit, push, open PRs, spawn agents, provision/deploy services, access credentials or alter swarm budget. Implement the host/server-controlled phase advance handler and trusted scheduler port. A public request-advance requires the verified host; internal authority callbacks use a separate trusted scheduler capability,never a body-supplied server actor. Check exact match/phase generation,server deadline and expected revision under the same transaction. Invoke completeDeadlineV1 and the canonical reducer to synthesize valid seeded missing crew votes,Route/Gate choices and power targets with timeout_vote/timeout_operation/target audit,then advance once. Persist checkpoint,events,receipt and publication outbox atomically; duplicate/late jobs or competing host requests cannot consume RNG/apply effects twice. Do not add Continue UI,client clock authority,provider scheduler configuration or any global pause. Store private timeout choices internally and project only allowed public evidence.
acceptance: Only verified host requests or trusted internal authority callbacks can trigger a phase transition after the engine-validated deadline.
Missing eligible votes,operator options and target selections are completed deterministically from the committed seed/action sequence and audit reason.
Duplicate jobs,stale phases and racing requests yield one transition with stable checkpoint/RNG/event/receipt results.
Tests cover early/late callbacks,host spoofing,backgrounded clients and timeout private data absent from public responses.
